title: A killed run's scratch is swept by the next run that asks for one
intention: A scratch directory or worktree left behind by a run that was killed before its atexit sweep could fire is removed by the next process that asks the scratch tool for one, so a killed run leaks only until the next proof starts instead of forever.
why: Measured 2026-10-08: /tmp held 1068 entries (1.7G on tmpfs). A clean bin/cairn test --exec of test_watch_receives_a_finding.py left its prefix at 254 before and 254 after, so the atexit door holds for runs that exit; the tester kills a timed-out proof (bf3c16162827) and a SIGKILL fires no atexit, so a killed run's scratch_dir and scratch_worktree leak forever. scratch.py's own docstring named the tail ('A run killed with SIGKILL fires no atexit hook and leaks'). CORRECTION measured after /sorted fired: not every leftover is a kill — exec_cwd_proof_fixture_* (55) and three other prefixes come from four proofs that call tempfile.mkdtemp bare, which test_scratch.py's corpus tooth caught red at this ticket's red-proof commit aaea6c36 (seal-red-cairn-tools-scratch); that is a separate defect in other components, not this door's.
traces_to: Law 4 (cleanup enforced by physics: the atexit door binds only runs that exit; a kill is the case it never reached) and the scratch charter's own falsifier 'if a scratch directory outlives its run' — measured red on the host today.
how: cairn/tools/scratch/scratch.py: scratch_dir and scratch_worktree put their owner's pid in the name behind a fixed marker (<prefix>scratch.<pid>-<mkdtemp suffix>); the first call in each process sweeps the temp root for marked entries whose pid is dead — rmtree, and for a worktree parent, prune the registration its worktree's .git file names. A live owner's entry is never touched; an unmarked entry is never touched. Mirrors the pid-in-the-name sweep of 201a37bf1613 (scratch tables) and isolation._sweep_orphaned_snapshots. New proof in cairn/tools/scratch/proofs.
falsifier: Falsifier: cairn/tools/scratch/proofs/test_a_killed_runs_scratch_is_swept_by_the_next.py (landed red), green and sealed under bin/cairn test --netns, teeth under PROVES for this ticket: (1) a SIGKILLed child's scratch_dir under a fixture TMPDIR is gone after the next process under that TMPDIR calls scratch_dir; (2) a SIGKILLed child's scratch_worktree is gone and the fixture repo's git worktree list no longer names it; (3) a live child's scratch_dir and an unmarked directory beside it survive that call; (4) an entry marked with another pid namespace and a pid that reads dead from here survives that call (peer F28). test_scratch.py, test_scratch_is_a_tool.py and tester's test_hollow.py stay green unchanged. Hollow: scratch.py reverted to the pre-build commit reds teeth 1 and 2 (measured); 3 and 4 are guards, green there because nothing is swept, and 4 is measured red at build against the sweep with its namespace check removed. Horizon: the temp root's marked entries with dead pids fall to zero after any proof run; the next host census of /tmp reads it.
watchme: none, because the live reading is the host temp root itself: /tmp entries matching scratch\.(\d+)-[a-z0-9_]{8}$ whose pid is dead, counted by the same regex in /home/akien/dev/src/cairn/cairn/tools/scratch/scratch.py, and every proof run's first scratch call sweeps them
children: none, because one sweep function, one name change in two doors, and one docstring paragraph in /home/akien/dev/src/cairn/cairn/tools/scratch/scratch.py, with its proof already landed
builder_notes: Questions a Haiku-level builder would need, answered: WHERE? cairn/tools/scratch/scratch.py only. (A) A module constant _MARK = 'scratch.' and a regex _OWNED = re.compile(r'scratch\.(\d+)-[a-z0-9_]{8}$'). (B) def _owner_alive(pid) as isolation._pid_alive (os.kill(pid, 0): ProcessLookupError -> False, PermissionError -> True) — copied, not imported (RULE 1). (C) def _sweep_dead_owners(tmp: str | None = None) -> list[str]: root = Path(tmp or tempfile.gettempdir()); for each entry in root.iterdir() (OSError -> return []), m = _OWNED.search(entry.name); skip unless m and entry.is_dir(); pid = int(m.group(1)); skip if pid == os.getpid() or _owner_alive(pid); if (entry / 'worktree' / '.git').is_file(): read its 'gitdir: X' line, rmtree entry, then git --git-dir <Path(X).parents[1]> worktree prune (env=git_env(), capture_output); else rmtree entry; append str(entry); any OSError prints 'scratch: could not sweep <entry>: ...' to stderr and continues. (D) A module flag _swept = False and def _sweep_once(): if not _swept: set it, call _sweep_dead_owners(). (E) scratch_dir: call _sweep_once() first, then mkdtemp(prefix=f'{prefix}{_MARK}{os.getpid()}-'). scratch_worktree: same, for the parent mkdtemp. (F) The module docstring's 'WHAT THIS DOES NOT CLAIM' paragraph is replaced by one citing 4784351e4838: a killed run leaks until the next process asks for a scratch, and the legacy unmarked entries are not this door's to judge. PROOF: already landed; it builds as written.

decisions.text: D1: the proof ALREADY LANDED in cairn commit aaea6c36 (red proof): cairn/tools/scratch/proofs/test_a_killed_runs_scratch_is_swept_by_the_next.py carries PROVES['4784351e4838'] keys '1'-'3'; teeth 1-2 measured red against today's scratch.py (a SIGKILLed child's scratch_dir and scratch_worktree outlive the next process's scratch_dir call), tooth 3 green as the guard. It builds as written — the build edits NO proof file, only cairn/tools/scratch/scratch.py (D2-D5).

D2: scratch.py gains module constants _MARK = 'scratch.' and _OWNED = re.compile(r'scratch\.(\d+)-[a-z0-9_]{8}$') (import re). scratch_dir makes its directory with tempfile.mkdtemp(prefix=f'{prefix}{_MARK}{os.getpid()}-'); scratch_worktree makes its parent the same way. Nothing else about either door changes: the atexit registration, ScratchPath, WorktreeUnavailable and the worktree path parent/'worktree' stay as they are.

D3: scratch.py gains def _owner_alive(pid: int) -> bool (os.kill(pid, 0); ProcessLookupError -> False; PermissionError -> True; else True — copied from isolation._pid_alive, not imported, RULE 1) and def _sweep_dead_owners(tmp: str | None = None) -> list[str]: root = Path(tmp or tempfile.gettempdir()); entries = list(root.iterdir()) (OSError -> return []); for each entry: m = _OWNED.search(entry.name); skip unless m and entry.is_dir(); pid = int(m.group(1)); skip if pid == os.getpid() or _owner_alive(pid); gitfile = entry / 'worktree' / '.git'; if gitfile.is_file(): gitdir = the text after 'gitdir:' on its first line, stripped; shutil.rmtree(entry); subprocess.run(['git', '--git-dir', str(Path(gitdir).parents[1]), 'worktree', 'prune'], capture_output=True, text=True, env=git_env()); else shutil.rmtree(entry); append str(entry). Every OSError (and a gitfile that does not parse) prints 'scratch: could not sweep {entry}: {type(e).__name__}: {e}' to stderr and continues; nothing raises.

D4: a module flag _swept = False and def _sweep_once() -> None: global _swept; if _swept: return; _swept = True; _sweep_dead_owners(). scratch_dir and scratch_worktree each call _sweep_once() as their FIRST statement, before mkdtemp. Once per process, at the first scratch call: no clock, no daemon. git_env is defined above scratch_worktree already; _sweep_dead_owners is placed after git_env so it can call it.

D5: the module docstring's 'WHAT THIS DOES NOT CLAIM' paragraph is replaced by one citing 4784351e4838: a run killed with SIGKILL fires no atexit hook, so its scratch carries its owner's pid in the name and the next process to ask for a scratch removes it (a worktree is also deregistered); no supervisor watches a directory; entries made before the marker existed carry no pid and are not this door's to judge. Verify through bin/cairn test --exec (pytest is refused): the new proof 3/3 green, then cairn/tools/scratch/proofs/test_scratch.py, cairn/tools/scratch/proofs/test_scratch_is_a_tool.py and cairn/devices/tester/proofs/test_hollow.py — the last two may carry the standing bare-mkdtemp red (seal-red-cairn-tools-scratch, four proofs in other components) and are judged tooth by tooth: every tooth green before the build stays green. Seal the new proof with bin/cairn test --netns --seal. The hollow reverts scratch.py; teeth 1-2 red there.

D6 (folds D5): the neighbours that carry the standing bare-mkdtemp red are cairn/tools/scratch/proofs/test_scratch.py (its tooth test_no_proof_in_this_repo_calls_mkdtemp_bare, red over four proofs in cairn/devices/tester and cairn/tools/base) and cairn/tools/scratch/proofs/test_scratch_is_a_tool.py (its tooth the_tool_stands runs test_scratch.py) — NOT test_hollow.py, which must be wholly green. Every other tooth of those two is green before the build and stays green after it.

D7 (folds D2 and D3, peer F28): the mark carries the pid namespace. A module constant _NS = os.stat('/proc/self/ns/pid').st_ino is read once at import. scratch_dir and scratch_worktree use mkdtemp(prefix=f'{prefix}{_MARK}{_NS}-{os.getpid()}-'), and _OWNED becomes re.compile(r'scratch\.(\d+)-(\d+)-[a-z0-9_]{8}$') with group 1 the namespace inode and group 2 the pid. In _sweep_dead_owners, an entry is judged only when int(m.group(1)) == _NS; an entry from any other namespace is skipped, never judged by its pid. Its pid is then int(m.group(2)), and everything else in D3 stands. The proof gains tooth 4 (test_an_entry_from_another_pid_namespace_survives_the_next_call, PROVES key '4'). It is green against today's scratch.py, which sweeps nothing. After the build it is measured red once against the sweep with its namespace check removed, then the check is restored, and the reading is recorded in measured_at_build.

D8 (settles pass-1 gap on D7): tooth 4's red is measured ONCE at build and is NOT a hollow criterion. After D2-D7 are built and the proof is 4/4 green, remove only the 'group1 == _NS' check from _sweep_dead_owners in the working tree, run bin/cairn test --exec '<venv python3> cairn/tools/scratch/proofs/test_a_killed_runs_scratch_is_swept_by_the_next.py' and keep its tooth-4 FAIL line, then git checkout -- cairn/tools/scratch/scratch.py so the build commit carries the check. The hollow (D5) reverts scratch.py to the pre-build commit, where tooth 4 is green because nothing is swept — so its criterion stays teeth 1-2 red. After PROVED, measured_at_build gains 'tooth4_red': the FAIL line verbatim and the edit that produced it.
